questions.title: Fever pathophysiology: hypothalamic set point resetting
questions.subject: fnd
questions.question: Which of the following pathophysiological mechanisms is fundamentally responsible for the development of a fever?

options.A: Decrease in the basal metabolic rate
options.C: Resetting of the hypothalamic thermoregulatory set point

explanations.A: Incorrect. Metabolic rate rises, rather than falls, during fever, as heat production is recruited to reach the newly elevated set point.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Sweat gland inactivation is a secondary contributor to reduced heat loss during the rising phase, not the fundamental mechanism, which lies at the level of the hypothalamic set point itself.
explanations.C: Correct. Pyrogens act on the hypothalamus to reset its thermoregulatory set point to a higher value; the hypothalamus then drives shivering and cutaneous vasoconstriction to raise core temperature until it matches this new, elevated target, which is the defining mechanism of fever. This is the same underlying mechanism regardless of which specific pathogen or paper describes it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Fever onset is associated with cutaneous vasoconstriction, which conserves heat, the opposite of vasodilation, which would promote heat loss.

questions.learning_objective: Explain fever as pyrogen-mediated resetting of the hypothalamic set point upward, and state that the ensuing shivering and vasoconstriction are the normal response to a body temperature that is now below the new set point.
